summary: Round 2. All three round-1 majors re-measured against the staged tree and all three are now KILLED: complete(pushes.get(i))->get(0) killed by eachConsumerIsCOMPLETEDWithITSOwnRunsAndNotAnothers; the assembling loop reduced to pushes.subList(0,1) killed by theAssemblingAdapterNotifiesOncePerRUNAndSharesONECopyOfTheBytes; relaxing BOTH halves of ByIdentity killed by TWOSubscribersThatCompareEQUALAreStillTWOConsumers. The author's contradiction of my round-1 ByIdentity finding is CORRECT and my finding is RETRACTED: measured, equals-alone (==  -> Objects.equals) SURVIVES the whole ingest suite and hashCode-alone (identityHashCode -> Objects.hashCode) SURVIVES; only the pair is catchable, so the record-with-generated-equals scenario I gave does not reach. Probes against the three NEW cases all died: per-push array copy (whole.clone()) killed by the isSameAs assertion, so isSameAs is load-bearing not incidental; swapped complete lists (pushes.get(size-1-i)) killed by the disjoint-run case; open(first push only), last-run-wins grouping, dropping the sink.failed guard, break-instead-of-continue on a failed sink, and zeroing firstOffset in the new push loop all killed. Existing-test edits are pure signature adaptation (open(Push)->open(List<Push>), push.via() -> pushes.forEach) with no assertion weakened. Three corrected javadocs verified true: LinkedHashMap->HashMap survives the suite as the comment now says; the INLINE/one-write-of-17-bytes claim in aSTREAMThatBROKE... matches FetchPolicy.modeFor with inlineCapBytes=Long.MAX_VALUE and writeHeldBytes issuing one write; and the new dedupe claim is true by measurement -- the same Subscriber subscribed twice to one RunKey yields one open with TWO pushes carrying the same key and firstOffset, and through assembling the consumer is invoked twice with the same key and offset. The red-record disclosure is right: without grouping, the equal-subscribers case and the per-consumer complete case both pass (each subscription is its own target, each completed with its own run), while the other three red against the ungrouped shape -- so two of five are correctly declared mutation-bound. Dependent modules still compile: every SubscriptionHub user outside ingest goes through assembling, whose signature is unchanged.

findings.title: The changed segmentFanOut semantics (consumers, not subscriptions) has no test that can fail
findings.failure_scenario: Mutation MEASURED SURVIVING: `new SegmentDelivery(heldBytes.length, true, targets.size(), false)` -> `new SegmentDelivery(heldBytes.length, true, 97, false)` passes the entire :ingest:test suite. The commit rewrites SegmentDelivery.java:80's @param segmentFanOut contract from 'once per subscription' to 'byte streams leaving the pod, one per consumer', and that is the half of M5.40a a future caller reads. A later change that reintroduces per-subscription counting (or multiplies by runs) is invisible to every test. It is honestly disclosed in the code comment and the backlog cell, and it is not testable through the present seam -- FetchPolicy is a final class, SegmentServing is a record taking it, and modeFor reads segmentFanOut only through wantsDirect, which this call site makes unreachable by hardcoding bytesInServingAz=true and servingPodUnderPressure=false -- so closing it means a seam change, not a test. Recording it so M5.43/M5.45b, which will make that branch reachable, inherit a named gap rather than a silent one.

findings.title: 'each single mutation is EQUIVALENT ON BEHAVIOUR' is right for the equals half and slightly too strong for the hashCode half
findings.failure_scenario: Measured: equals-alone survives (different identity hash codes put the two subscribers in different buckets, so the relaxed equals is never called) and that one really is equivalent short of an identity-hash collision, which no test can arrange. hashCode-alone survives the suite too, but it is not behaviourally equivalent: System.identityHashCode never throws and never changes, while Objects.hashCode(subscriber) calls caller-supplied code inside publishSegment's grouping loop, which nothing wraps. A subscriber whose hashCode throws (a record holding a self-referential list, for instance) would escape publishSegment as a RuntimeException, and DefaultIngest.pushLoop swallows it -- the whole delta's delivery dropped silently, where identityHashCode cannot fail. No test pins that, and I am not asking for one; the javadoc's 'equivalent on behaviour' should read 'unobservable through merging', which is what was actually measured. Prose only, in a file whose other three corrected claims all check out.
